issue_context.title: Weatherflow Sensors Stop Updating
issue_context.body:
### The problem

I am using the new Weatherflow integration, and after some time (as short has 15 minutes), the data in the Weatherflow sensors stop receiving updates.  The weather station is transmitting data during this time, because the online cloud has data during these periods and if I restart HA the data starts flowing again (temporarily). There is nothing containing "weatherflow" in my HA log output.

In the following screenshot, here is temperature data that has not updated for 18 hours.  I restarted HA prior to 3pm on the graph, where data briefly flows until it stays at the last reading.
![Screenshot from 2023-10-18 09-07-11](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/assets/349445/a02add53-f764-4cdc-b708-aefcfecbe4f3)

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2023.10.3

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

@jeeftor The `sensor_status` on my device is most likely because my device is on "Power Saver" mode due to low battery.  In this mode it does still send out updates, just at a lower frequency.  The integration shouldn't stop updating.
Not to pile on, but I'm seeing the same issue.  After a restart I received updates for a while (8 hours last time) and then it just stops updating.

> @jeeftor The `sensor_status` on my device is most likely because my device is on "Power Saver" mode due to low battery. In this mode it does still send out updates, just at a lower frequency. The integration shouldn't stop updating.

This might be the problem. Mine switched to Mode 2 briefly and I believe it’s when the integration stopped updating.

Mode 2 is when the Tempest sends data at 1 minute intervals.

Here are the modes explained:

https://help.weatherflow.com/hc/en-us/articles/360048877194-Solar-Power-Rechargeable-Battery
I can confirm the same, my tempest went to mode 2 early in the morning and that is approximately when I stopped collecting data.
Same thing for me.
I wonder if it prioritizes sending TCP to the cloud over UDP when things get "low"... Maybe somebody can reach out to support. Also looks like we should add a PowerSave Mode sensor...

I too have had problems with it stopping to report, especially during the night (assuming again low battery situation discussed above), the interesting piece is that I have a docker container of weatherflow2mqtt running and it continues to get updates over UDP.

I don’t think there’s any traffic priority depending on the mode the Tempest is in. After all it’s the hub that’s doing all the broadcasting and that is either on or off and other UDP integrations continue to work as expected.

My theory would be that the hub sends something when the mode changes and this integration misinterprets the received packet and hangs.

And yes, a mode sensor would be a very welcome addition.
@natekspencer  - you ever seen stuff like this drop out?
The only other idea I have which is annoying is to turn on debug info for: pyweatherflowudp And then we can look at the last message you got

> @natekspencer - you ever seen stuff like this drop out?

Very early on with the UDP library I hadn't accounted for null values in the library and it broke it. There might be something similar here with the integration
